b2-paraguay-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Languages
b2-paraguay-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Paraguay, and he thinks Spanish is the only official language.
b2-paraguay-01.prompt: Correct Carlos with a stance adverb.
b2-paraguay-01.target: En realidad, Paraguay tiene dos lenguas oficiales: el español y el guaraní.
b2-paraguay-01.english: In fact, Paraguay has two official languages: Spanish and Guaraní.
b2-paraguay-01.canDo: I can correct an assumption about Guaraní and Spanish with stance adverbs such as *en realidad* and *en rigor*.

b2-paraguay-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Views of the Missions
b2-paraguay-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about the Jesuit missions, and she asks what historians say.
b2-paraguay-02.prompt: Tell Meg two views of the missions, joined by a contrast connector.
cues: Add the opposite view, with a connector
b2-paraguay-02.target: Según algunos historiadores, las misiones protegieron a los guaraníes; sin embargo, otros dicen que los jesuitas controlaban su vida.
b2-paraguay-02.english: According to some historians, the missions protected the Guaraní; however, others say the Jesuits controlled their lives.
b2-paraguay-02.canDo: I can set two views of the Jesuit missions side by side with *sin embargo*, *no obstante* and *aunque*.

b2-paraguay-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Fortress of Humaitá
b2-paraguay-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are giving a short talk about the Triple Alliance War, and Carlos asks about the fortress of Humaitá.
b2-paraguay-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the fortress and when.
cues: Say what happened to the fortress
b2-paraguay-03.target: La fortaleza de Humaitá fue tomada por las fuerzas aliadas en 1868.
b2-paraguay-03.english: The fortress of Humaitá was taken by the allied forces in 1868.
b2-paraguay-03.canDo: I can say what was signed, taken or occupied in the Triple Alliance War with *ser* + participle.

b2-paraguay-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Mennonites in the Chaco
b2-paraguay-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are talking about the Chaco, and you want to add a side remark.
b2-paraguay-04.prompt: Add a short side remark about the Mennonites.
cues: Mark it as a side remark
b2-paraguay-04.target: A propósito de los menonitas, llegaron al Chaco en 1927.
b2-paraguay-04.english: Speaking of the Mennonites, they arrived in the Chaco in 1927.
b2-paraguay-04.canDo: I can add a side remark about the Chaco with *por cierto* or *a propósito de* and come back to my point.

b2-paraguay-05.title: Communicative Challenge: The Guampa
b2-paraguay-05.scenario: You are Meg. You watched a documentary about tereré, and Carlos asks what a guampa is.
b2-paraguay-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the guampa is, with a relative clause.
cues: Say that it is a cup
Say what is served in it
b2-paraguay-05.target: La guampa es el vaso en el que se sirve el tereré.
b2-paraguay-05.english: The guampa is the cup in which tereré is served.
b2-paraguay-05.canDo: I can describe tereré and the guarania with *en el que*, *con la que* and *del que*.

b2-paraguay-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Paraguay in Brief
b2-paraguay-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You are preparing a short talk about Paraguay, and Meg asks you to try one sentence on the languages.
b2-paraguay-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg one exact fact about Guaraní, with a stance adverb.
cues: Say since when it is official
b2-paraguay-consolidation.target: En rigor, el guaraní es lengua oficial desde 1992.
b2-paraguay-consolidation.english: Strictly speaking, Guaraní has been an official language since 1992.
b2-paraguay-consolidation.canDo: I can correct an assumption about Guaraní and Spanish with stance adverbs such as *en realidad* and *en rigor*.
